title: Clearing shifts on a lead change removes shifts by their timing
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Work Orders page on the build under test, signed in with permission to reassign work orders and to edit the Schedule.
  2. A work order (for example S2-17578) has a current lead technician (for example Jeremy).
  3. On the Schedule, that technician has three shifts on this work order: one that has already ended, one that has not started yet, and one that is under way right now (for example Jeremy's shift runs 8:00 to 12:00 and it is now 10:00).
  4. At least one other lead technician (for example Dana) is available.
custom_steps:
1. Reassign the work order's lead technician to the other technician (for example Dana).
  2. When the prompt asks, choose to clear shifts.
  3. Open the Schedule and read what happened to each of the three shifts: the one that had ended, the one not yet started, and the one under way.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • When the user chooses to clear shifts: an already-ended shift stays as it is; a not-yet-started shift is removed; a shift under way at the moment of the lead change is ended at that moment (the part already under way stays, the rest is removed) - e.g. Jeremy 8:00-12:00 with the lead changing to Dana at 10:00 leaves Jeremy 8:00-10:00.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10047 — Reassign or unassign the lead technician. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S4-R25 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R25: “When the user chooses to clear shifts: a shift that has already ended stays as it is; a shift that has not started yet is removed; a shift that is under way at the moment of the lead change is ended at that moment, so the part already under way stays on the schedule and the rest is removed. Example: Jeremy’s shift runs 8:00 to 12:00 and the lead changes to Dana at 10:00; Jeremy’s shift now runs 8:00 to 10:00.”
